transcript.text: my oven fan keeps going after ive turned the oven off, been about 20 mins now. is it broken??

It is very likely not broken. Most ovens have a dedicated cooling fan that keeps running for 10–30 minutes (sometimes longer) after you switch off to cool down the electronics and controls behind the panel. This is normal behaviour. However, we need to make sure it isn't stuck on because of an overheating issue or a faulty thermostat. Please check two things: 1. Does the fan eventually stop once the oven is completely cold (e.g., after an hour)?
2. Are the control knobs or the fascia panel around them getting unusually hot? If the fan stops when cool and the controls aren't hot, it's just doing its job. If it never stops even when cold, or if the controls are scorching hot, there may be a fault with the cooling fan motor or its thermostat.

yes it does stop on its own, usually after about 20-30 mins, today it went on longer after a long roast. the door and top of the oven are still warm but im not sure about the knobs, i havent really noticed if they're hot

That suggests it is doing exactly what it should. The fact that it stops on its own after 20–30 minutes (and ran a bit longer today because the oven was hotter) means the thermal cut-out or thermostat controlling the fan is working correctly. It is very common for this to run longer after a long roast, as there is more heat stored in the cavity and insulation. As long as the fan eventually stops when cool and the fascia/controls aren't too hot to touch comfortably, your oven is fine. If you want to help it cool down slightly faster next time, just make sure the vents around the top of the oven or behind the fascia (if accessible) aren't blocked by cabinetry or clutter. Otherwise, no action needed.
